issues.description: Guard fires for every non-Tab key, not just Enter/Return, broadening dismiss behavior unintentionally.
issues.detail: The branch sits inside the Enter/Return handler but only excludes Tab, so any non-Tab key reaching this code hides the popup and re-dispatches. The intended invariant is 'when Enter-accept is off, treat Enter as a normal keystroke'; narrow the guard to Return/Enter explicitly.

issues.description: keyPressEvent complects config lookup, key classification, and hide+forward side effect in one unreasoned branch.
issues.detail: The predicate `not self.get_conf(...) and not key == Qt.Key_Tab` mixes three concerns without a stated invariant. Extract a small predicate or represent accept-keys as data (e.g., `{Tab}` vs `{Tab, Enter, Return}`), and state the precondition/postcondition so the dismissal is provably sound.

issues.description: `not key == Qt.Key_Tab` is awkward; write `key != Qt.Key_Tab` or name the accept-key set.
issues.detail: The negated equality reads as transcription rather than reasoning and relies on Python precedence folklore. The familiar `key != Qt.Key_Tab` is clearer; better still, name the set of accept keys explicitly so the rule is data rather than a buried conditional.

issues.description: `get_conf` called on every keystroke inside the popup's hot keyPressEvent path.
issues.detail: Reading configuration through the plugin conf system on every key event complects a slow-changing preference with fast-changing keystrokes. Read once at popup show and cache on `self`, or subscribe to changes; the event handler should be about keys, not config lookup.

issues.description: Default `use_enter_for_completions: True` added without a stated config-migration invariant.
issues.detail: Adding the key to defaults preserves behavior only if absent-key lookups return True for legacy profiles and CONF_VERSION handling is correct. Confirm the conf-version bump or document that existing users transparently inherit the new default; otherwise upgraders may silently get different behavior.

issues.description: No test or stated specification exhibits either branch of the new option.
issues.detail: The PR ships a behavioral switch with no automated test. State the precondition (option False, popup visible, Enter pressed) and the postcondition under both branches, and add a test that exercises Enter-accepts-vs-newline so future regressions are caught.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the change is small and well-intentioned but UNDER-AUDITED: the new guard in keyPressEvent intertwines a config read, a negated key check, and a hide-and-forward side effect without a stated invariant. The most substantive concern is that the branch fires for any non-Tab key rather than just Return/Enter, broadening dismissal behavior unintentionally. Secondary issues are stylistic-but-symptomatic (`not key == Qt.Key_Tab`), hot-path config reads, missing tests, and an unverified config-migration story. Acceptable after narrowing the key check, separating decision from action, and adding a test exhibiting both branches.
